reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 28 question-paper pages and PDF pages 1–21 of the combined Ordinary Level scheme (cover, notes, contents, the Paper 1 scale table on page 5, the summary of mark allocations on page 6, the annotation palette on page 7, every Paper 1 model solution and marking note on pages 8–20, and the Paper 2 title page 21). Each task boundary is the published scale beside its model solution, cross-checked against the printed summary.
sourceNotes: The 2020 Leaving Certificate examinations were cancelled and replaced by Calculated Grades, but the SEC published this paper and its marking scheme. The paper is 300 marks: candidates answer all nine questions (Section A Q1–6, 25 marks each; Section B Q7 35 marks, Q8 55 marks, Q9 60 marks). Every question is retained.
40 independently marked units, matching the printed summary of allocations on scheme page 6. Q3(a)(i) and (a)(ii) share one 10D scale (“4 items (find z₃ and 3 plots)”) and are one task.

Paper 1 bands from the Ordinary Level scale table on scheme page 5: 5B 0,2,5; 5C 0,3,4,5; 5D 0,2,3,4,5; 10B 0,5,10; 10C 0,4,8,10; 10D 0,3,5,8,10; 15D 0,5,7,11,15 (the Ordinary Level 15D ladder differs from the Higher Level 0,4,7,11,15, and Q2(b) prints “Scale 15D (0, 5, 7, 11,15)”).

This paper had no authored cards before this review; all 40 units are new. Marking points are lifted line by line from the scheme (read through the glyph repair map) and labelled with the part of the scheme they come from. Q5(b)(ii)–(iii) are graph tasks whose model solutions are drawings; their cards carry the printed credit criteria and point to the scheme pages.
The question booklet is LC003GLP100EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003GLP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 2. All page references are PDF positions, which match the printed scheme page numbers.

cards.stem: In the 2016 Summer Olympics, Michael Phelps, won the 200 m Butterfly final in a time of 1 minute and 53·36 seconds (1: 53·36). The time it took to swim each of the four 50 m sections of the race (split time) is given in the table below. The percentage increase in the time taken to swim one section is also given. Thus, it took the swimmer 14·7% longer to swim the second 50 metres compared to the first 50 metres. Race Section, Split Time (secs), Percentage Increase: 0 – 50 m, 24·85; 50 – 100 m, 28·5, 14·7%; 100 – 150 m, 29·33; 150 – 200 m, 30·68; Total, 1:53·36.
cards.questionText: Complete the table by finding the percentage increase in split time by comparing each split time with the previous one. Give your answers correct to one decimal place.
